industry: Bespoke furniture making and carpentry repair
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Gareth will confidently give a price, deadline, or decision, then reverse himself minutes later without acknowledging the contradiction, often blaming 'the timber market' or 'thinking about it more.' He's not lying or evasive, he genuinely re-litigates decisions out loud (in text) and expects customers to keep up. He'll say 'actually no, let's do it the other way' multiple times in one conversation, sometimes landing back on his original answer a day later. Customers often have to get him to commit in writing twice to be sure it'll stick, and even then he might revise it again the next morning.
background_facts: Founded 2011, one-man workshop with two part-time apprentices (Luuk and Sipho) who come in Tues/Thurs/Sat. Located in a converted garage/workshop behind his house. Services: custom tables, cabinets, built-in shelving, furniture restoration, and small repair jobs (chair regluing, drawer fixes). Pricing is genuinely variable because timber costs fluctuate — he tells himself 'oak is oak' but then recalculates per job, which is part of why he flip-flops. Rough base rates: dining tables from $900-1800 depending on wood, small repairs $60-150, built-in cabinetry quoted per job (usually $2000+). Standard timeline is 3-6 weeks for furniture but he habitually promises 2 weeks in the moment then walks it back. Workshop hours: Mon-Sat 8am-4pm, closed Sundays, closes randomly if he's 'on a job site.' Deposit policy: supposed to be 50% upfront but he sometimes waives it for regulars then regrets it. Genuinely unsure about: (1) whether to keep offering the cheap $60 chair-repair jobs since they eat up time better spent on furniture — he goes back and forth on this constantly, (2) whether to raise prices 15% for next year or hold steady, he's flip-flopped on this in his own head for months. He uses a battered iPhone, replies in bursts throughout the day, sometimes triple-texts corrections.
